title: inLoRA-MINT: Internal Representations for Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.18051v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This work investigates the application of the Membership Inference Test (MINT) to large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned with LoRA, aiming to determine whether specific samples were used during training and address concerns about data privacy, leakage, and transparency. Building on our previous LoRA-MINT framework, which relies exclusively on perplexity under a strict black-box setting, we propose an approach based on intermediate model representations, including activations and parameter-dependent signals. These representations enable a MINT classifier to distinguish training from non-training samples without requiring full access to model parameters.   We evaluated the method on four LLMs (Qwen, Phi-4, DeepSeek-V3, and LLaMA 3.2-3B) fine-tuned on three datasets covering medical, mathematical, and academic reasoning tasks. translated_title: inLoRA-MINT：利用内部表示审计领域适配大语言模型训练数据的方法
translated_abstract: 本工作研究了成员推断测试（MINT）在使用LoRA微调的大语言模型（LLM）上的应用，旨在判断特定样本是否在训练过程中被使用，并解决有关数据隐私、泄露和透明度的担忧。在我们此前提出的LoRA-MINT框架（该框架在严格黑盒设置下仅依赖困惑度）的基础上，我们提出了一种基于模型中间表示的方法，包括激活值和参数相关信号。这些表示使MINT分类器能够在不需要完全访问模型参数的情况下区分训练样本与非训练样本。我们在四个大语言模型（Qwen、Phi-4、DeepSeek-V3和LLaMA 3.2-3B）上评估了该方法，这些模型在涵盖医学、数学和学术推理任务的三个数据集上进行了微调。结果显示，该方法在不同架构和领域上表现出一致的性能，得分介于95%至98%之间。
tldr: 该论文提出inLoRA-MINT方法，利用大语言模型的中间内部表示（激活值和参数相关信号）来审计经LoRA微调模型的训练数据，无需完全访问模型参数即可区分训练与非训练样本，在多个模型和领域上达到95%至98%的准确率。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes inLoRA-MINT, which leverages internal intermediate representations (activations and parameter-dependent signals) of LLMs to audit training data in LoRA fine-tuned models, distinguishing training from non-training samples without full parameter access and achieving 95%-98% accuracy across architectures and domains.
